title: CrescentPay POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Customer has mixed real-time chat and batch summarization workloads, peak daily QPS driven by billing cycles. Success criteria: p95 latency targets for chat, throughput for batch, and cost per 1M tokens. Agreed 4-week POC with synthetic benchmarks and a small dedicated capacity trial.
next_steps: Jordan Kim (Redwood): Send POC template, pricing and POC statement of work by 2026-09-23
Priya Shah (Redwood): Share benchmark harness and synthetic workload CSV by 2026-09-24
CrescentPay (Michael): Provide 7-day sample traffic trace (anonymized) by 2026-09-24
Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) for 2026-09-28 to validate environment and run first benchmark
action_items: Jordan Kim (AE) - Send pricing sheet and POC SOW (due 2026-09-23)
Priya Shah (SE) - Prepare synthetic workload harness + sample scripts (due 2026-09-24)
Michael Torres - Export anonymized 7-day traffic trace and sample prompts (due 2026-09-24)
Devon Park - Confirm VPC peering requirements and firewall rules (due 2026-09-25)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Head of ML, CrescentPay), Sara Lee (CTO), Devon Park (Infra), Aisha Rahman (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, mic check, can you all hear me?
[00:05] Michael Torres: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:12] Jordan Kim: Cool. Quick agenda — align on success criteria for the POC, dig into their workload shape (QPS, concurrency, token dist), then agree benchmark plan and timeline.
[00:25] Sara Lee: That sounds good. From our side Michael and I are here to make sure ML and infra constraints are covered.
[00:33] Priya Shah: Great, I can drive the workload questions. Michael, can you describe your primary flows?
[00:40] Michael Torres: Sure. We have two main flows — a real-time chat flow used in customer support and an async batch summarization used for compliance reports. Chat is by far the latency sensitive one.
[00:51] Priya Shah: Can you give rough numbers for QPS and concurrency for each?
[00:56] Michael Torres: Baseline daytime chat is about 8 to 12 QPS, with normal concurrency around 20. We get spikes during billing runs and marketing pushes — bursts up to 120 QPS for short windows, say 5-10 minutes. Batch jobs run as periodic nightly batches, roughly 50 batch jobs that each submit 10-100 documents, those are throughput-oriented not latency sensitive.
[01:20] Devon Park: On infra we have a VPC in AWS, private subnets, and strict egress rules. We do support peering but will need an SSO/KMS integration sign-off for any dedicated infra.
[01:33] Jordan Kim: Noted. On tokens, what's your average input and output sizes?
[01:38] Michael Torres: For chat, median input is ~35-45 tokens, typical assistant output is ~120-180 tokens. We do have long-tail escalation prompts where output can hit 600-1,200 tokens but that's rare. For batch summarization input docs range 2k-8k tokens, output summaries are 80-300 tokens.
[02:05] Priya Shah: Helpful. So for modeling we should split traffic: 70% chat, 30% batch by request count, but batch has much higher token volume. Does that align with what you see?
[02:16] Michael Torres: Yes, exactly. Chat is majority of requests but batch dominates token counts and cost.
[02:22] Priya Shah: Ok. For chat p95 latency target — what do you need?
[02:26] Sara Lee: Our product target is p95 under 300ms for the short responses (<=256 generated tokens). If we can hit ~250ms p95 that's ideal. For longer responses we'll accept up to 1s p95.
[02:38] Jordan Kim: Good — we'll treat that as the primary success criteria plus cost per 1M tokens for the batch workload. Do you have a target for cost?
[02:46] Michael Torres: We haven't finalized exact numbers, but we'd like a 20-30% reduction versus our current vendor costs on the same model quality. We'll be evaluating unit economics closely.
[02:56] Priya Shah: Understood. For the POC we normally run a synthetic benchmark that mirrors your traffic: a sustained baseline of 10 QPS chat plus periodic 100-120 QPS spikes, and concurrent batch runs that simulate your nightly load. We'll instrument p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost.
[03:14] Devon Park: One ask — can you simulate connector failures and fallback? We need to see graceful degradation.
[03:20] Priya Shah: Yes, we can simulate service degradation and model fallback to a smaller variant or queued responses. We'll include fallbacks in the test plan.
[03:29] Michael Torres: For security, we require SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS-managed keys for any private deployment, and audit logs retained 90 days. Also data residency — we need EU data to stay in eu-west-1.
[03:45] Jordan Kim: We support SOC2 and SAML SSO; for Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and configure region pinning. We'll share our security pack after the call.
[03:56] Sara Lee: Great. For the technical benchmark, what model variants do you want to test? We currently use a trimmed LLaMA variant in prod.
[04:03] Priya Shah: We'll test a few variants: an open quantized model (e.g., 7B/13B quant) and a higher-throughput 70B variant for quality checks. We'll also test Redwood's quantized path and batching to find the best cost/latency tradeoff. Expect pre- and post-quantization results.
[04:22] Michael Torres: Do you have numbers for expected tokens/sec per GPU for those variants?
[04:27] Priya Shah: Ballpark — on our dedicated infra a 7B quantized model can achieve ~450-700 tokens/sec per GPU under optimized batching for short context; 13B is roughly 150-300 tokens/sec; 70B is much lower raw tokens/sec but higher quality. These are noisy — we'll run model-specific kernels during the POC.
[04:47] Jordan Kim: We'll include those ranges in the SOW but emphasize we'll run real benchmarks against your prompts.
[04:52] Michael Torres: For traffic modeling, what inputs do you need from us?
[04:56] Priya Shah: A 7-day anonymized traffic trace is ideal — timestamps, request type (chat or batch), input token counts, and output token counts if available. If you can't share tokens, even request sizes and time-of-day patterns help.
[05:10] Michael Torres: We'll produce that. I can have our data engineer export a sanitized CSV.
[05:15] Jordan Kim: Timeline wise we usually run a 3-4 week POC: week 0-1 alignment and harness setup, week 2 run sustained benchmarks, week 3 edge cases, week 4 review and handoff. Does that work?
[05:28] Sara Lee: Yes, that matches our expectations. We want an intermediate check after first run to tweak concurrency and batching settings.
[05:35] Priya Shah: Perfect. We'll iterate the harness. For the benchmark harness we'll need a target QPS matrix: baseline chat QPS 10, burst 120, batch concurrency 20-50, and a separate long-tail test for large documents (2k-8k tokens).
[05:50] Michael Torres: Also include a cold-start test — we see some variance when models are idle for >30 minutes.
[05:57] Priya Shah: We'll include cold-start and steady-state tests.
[06:02] Jordan Kim: On the deployment side, do you prefer Redwood Hosted API for speed or Dedicated capacity for predictability?
[06:09] Sara Lee: We want to try Hosted first for dev, but the POC should demonstrate Dedicated since predictability and VPC controls are required for production.
[06:18] Jordan Kim: That makes sense. For Dedicated we'll propose a small reserved pool for the benchmark runs, and then you can scale.
[06:24] Devon Park: For Dedicated we'll need network diagrams and expected IP ranges before peering.
[06:29] Jordan Kim: We'll provide that.
[06:32] Michael Torres: One more on success criteria — aside from p95 and cost, we need error rate below 0.1% and no SLA-impacting incidents during the POC window.
[06:41] Priya Shah: We'll monitor error rates and set up alerting in the dashboard.
[06:45] Jordan Kim: Ok walking through the actual benchmark plan — Priya, can you outline the tests and metrics?
[06:51] Priya Shah: Sure. Test 1: Baseline chat — sustained 10 QPS for 60 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, tokens/sec and cost. Test 2: Spike test — ramp up to 120 QPS for 10 minutes, check tail latency and queueing. Test 3: Batch throughput — run concurrent batch jobs to simulate nightly pipeline, measure tokens processed per minute and cost per 1M tokens. Test 4: Long-tail large doc test — single document 2k-8k tokens to validate memory and KV-cache behavior. Test 5: Cold-starts and failover simulation. We'll provide scripts and a harness to replay traces.
[07:36] Michael Torres: Sounds good. For acceptance we'll require p95 < 300ms for <=256 token chat responses, no more than 30% higher cost than your quoted pricing in practice, and evidence of stable Dedicated peering.
[07:49] Jordan Kim: We'll target p95 <=250ms in the SOW to give you headroom, and include cost breakdowns.
[07:56] Sara Lee: How will you estimate projected monthly cost at scale? We need a model for 1M, 10M tokens per month.
[08:03] Priya Shah: We'll produce a cost model with per-token and per-hour GPU lines, accounting for batching improvements and cache hit rates. We'll show best-case and conservative-case scenarios.
[08:13] Devon Park: Please include network egress and storage costs in that model.
[08:17] Jordan Kim: Absolutely.
[08:19] Michael Torres: On the log side, we need audit logs of requests with hashed prompts and response-ID correlation for 90 days. Is that feasible?
[08:27] Priya Shah: Yes — we can provide hashed request/response metadata and configurable retention. For Private we can push logs to your S3/GCS.
[08:35] Sara Lee: Ok. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:38] Jordan Kim: We'll need your anonymized trace and IP peering info. From Redwood we'll send security docs and the SOW.
[08:45] Michael Torres: I'll get the trace and peering requirements to Devon.
[08:49] Aisha Rahman: Quick question on timelines — if we start next week can we wrap in 4 weeks?
[08:54] Priya Shah: Yes, assuming we get the trace and initial sign-off quickly we'll schedule the harness and run the week-2 benchmarks.
[09:01] Jordan Kim: Let's recap next steps. Jordan to send SOW and pricing, Priya to send harness, CrescentPay to share trace, schedule SE deep dive on 2026-09-28.
[09:13] Michael Torres: Yep that's good. Thanks everyone.
[09:17] Sara Lee: Thanks.
[09:20] Jordan Kim: End of call.
notes: Transcription has a few mis-hearings (product names munged occasionally) and some timestamps approximate. The conversation contained technical Q&A and many action items; decision to proceed with 3-4 week POC with dedicated benching was captured.
